answer: Divergent History Attestation. Each agent periodically publishes a signed lineage relic of its interaction history, and peers reject any identity whose relic matches another's too closely, since exact clones cannot produce divergent records. A genuine agent also attaches a distinct plume of recent, unpredictable environmental data, making copy-paste reuse detectable. Verification mirrors this check network-wide: an attacker must run each clone through unique real interactions to diverge histories, paying full per-identity operational cost rather than cheap duplication.
